citation: Lui ID, Law TWS, Chung CL, Wong SSY, So WWY, Lee J, Yip PSF. Development and evaluation of a mental health and suicide prevention student leadership training programme for secondary school students in Hong Kong. BMC Pediatrics. Published online 5 Jan 2026. doi:10.1186/s12887-025-06461-3.
title: Development and evaluation of a mental health and suicide prevention student leadership training programme for secondary school students in Hong Kong
abstract: Evaluation of the S.H.I.E.L.D.S. school-based programme, which trained Hong Kong secondary-school student leaders as mental-health gatekeepers and supported student-led mental-health promotion activities.
population: secondary school student leaders in Hong Kong
secondary school general students in Hong Kong
school staff advisors in Hong Kong
setting: S.H.I.E.L.D.S. programme rounds, June 2022 to June 2023
intervention_or_exposure: S.H.I.E.L.D.S. student mental-health gatekeeper and leadership programme
outcomes: gatekeeper self-efficacy and perceived ability to help peers
help-seeking willingness and school social environment
uncertainty: No randomized control group was used in this programme evaluation.
Several quantitative outcomes showed small or non-significant changes despite positive qualitative feedback.

evidence_claims.statement: Across 89 student leaders, 33 staff advisors and 423 general students from eight schools, quantitative analyses reported no significant overall changes in student leaders’ and general students’ mental-health knowledge and attitudes, while qualitative feedback was more positive.
evidence_claims.population: secondary school student leaders in Hong Kong
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: S.H.I.E.L.D.S. student mental-health gatekeeper and leadership programme

provenance.source_span: The abstract reports participant counts and a null overall quantitative pattern for knowledge/attitudes, alongside positive qualitative feedback.

evidence_claims.statement: Student leaders and staff described perceived gains in leaders’ mental-health knowledge and ability to help peers, but these self-reported qualitative findings should not be treated as causal evidence of improved clinical outcomes.
evidence_claims.population: secondary school student leaders in Hong Kong
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: S.H.I.E.L.D.S. student mental-health gatekeeper and leadership programme
evidence_claims.outcome: gatekeeper self-efficacy and perceived ability to help peers

provenance.source_span: Qualitative feedback indicated that leaders perceived improvements in knowledge and ability to help peers; staff observations were directionally similar.

evidence_claims.statement: The authors note that the relatively short programme duration may have limited measurable changes and recommend longer-duration and longitudinal evaluation.
evidence_claims.population: secondary school student leaders in Hong Kong
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: S.H.I.E.L.D.S. student mental-health gatekeeper and leadership programme

provenance.source_span: The manuscript explicitly identifies short programme duration as a limitation and calls for longer and longitudinal follow-up.

limitations: Pre-post programme evaluation without a randomized control group.
Quantitative and qualitative results were not uniformly aligned.
The study evaluated knowledge, attitudes, help-giving and implementation outcomes rather than suicide mortality.
applicability: Useful for school-based mental-health promotion and gatekeeper-programme design in Hong Kong secondary schools.
Does not by itself establish an effect on suicide attempts or suicide mortality.
safety_boundaries: Do not infer an individual student’s suicide risk from these programme-level findings.
Do not present programme acceptability or self-efficacy changes as evidence of reduced suicide mortality.
